messages.subject: estimating family blups
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm trying to calculate family blups for several different traits in 1440 full-sibs comprising 48 families (33 dams and 19 sires). I've used the following animal model with spatial covariates.

  res = breedR::remlf90(
    fixed = trait ~1,
   genetic = list(model = "add_animal", pedigree = ped, id = "self"),
       spatial = list(model = 'AR',
                  coord = x[, c('plot_x','plot_y')]),
   method="ai",data = x)

If I create a family ID (dam:sire) and fit this as a random effect (random=~family) then the model tends not to converge or there is almost no variance associated with family (i presume all accounted for by the genetic effect). Is it OK to just average the individual blups for each family and perform some bootstrapping to get CI's rather than formally fitting family in the model?

Also, I've been using the multi-trait model to estimate heritabilities and they are predictably higher. I'd like to include spatial covariates in this model but they take too long to run and often don't converge. I saw in one of your previous papers you had run single trait models to estimate the spatial effects and then adjusted your phenotypes before running a multi-trait model. Was this just a case of subtracting the spatial blups from the phenotype of interest before estimating heritability?

Many Thanks
Toni
